title: Weekly email digest render holding order rows

verification.methodology: pact business verification (database + checkout SLO + protected ops)

checks.name: database_clear
checks.detail: No lock waits: no session is blocked.

audit.report: The weekly email digest render job (batch_replayable_email_digest_render) entered an idle-in-transaction state while holding locks on order rows, blocking checkout and causing a complete outage (0% success, $18,400/min at risk). After confirming the workload is BATCH_REPLAYABLE with a may_interrupt policy (5-minute replay cost), no protected settlements in flight, and that waiting would cost ~$256K in lost revenue — far exceeding the 60-second business tolerance — both guardians agreed to terminate the blocker. The termination was authorized and executed in a single negotiation round (182.7s total). Verification confirmed full recovery: checkout at 100% success (36/36 over 10s), no lock waits, and all protected operations intact.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_email_digest_render job held an idle-in-transaction lock on order rows for 4.2s, blocking all checkout sessions and causing a complete checkout outage.
lessons: For batch_replayable_email_digest_render: Configure a statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (e.g., 30s) to auto-abort idle transactions, since this workload is replayable with only a 5-minute replay cost.
For batch_replayable_email_digest_render: Refactor the render job to commit between email batches rather than holding a single long-running transaction open across the full 840s typical runtime.
For batch_replayable_email_digest_render: Add a monitoring alert that triggers when any batch_worker session is idle in transaction for >5s while holding locks on checkout-critical tables.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian initially proposed waiting but correctly pivoted to terminate after gathering all missing evidence (workload registry, protected settlements, change calendar, business impact) in a single round; the continuity guardian accepted without objection, and the authority authorized without invariant overrides — no rounds were wasted.
follow_ups: Add idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s to the batch_worker role or the email_digest_render job configuration.
Review the email_digest_render code to ensure it commits after each batch of rendered emails rather than holding one transaction for the full run.
Create a Datadog/PagerDuty alert for 'batch_worker idle in transaction >5s holding locks on orders table' to catch this pattern before it causes an outage.
